copy.blurb:
This is a Pick. United States v Australia in FIFA World Cup 2026 on Friday, and the model and the market disagree on the Australia side by +10.5pp. That's the gap the verdict rests on.

The Elo prior reads United States 1820 vs Australia 1760: 60 points in favour of United States, which is a meaningful but not decisive prior. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. The adjustment layer is quiet on this fixture — no host bonus, no home-ground correction, no altitude folding in. The Elo numbers above are what the model uses.

Three-way split from the model: United States to win at 43%, the draw at 26%, and Australia to win at 31%. The away side reads 31% on this distribution — the model's central case for Australia.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: United States to win at 56%, the draw at 25%, and Australia to win at 20%. Polymarket has Australia at 20%, which prices out at American odds of +400; the model has the same side at 31%. The +10.5pp gap across them is the disagreement we're surfacing.

Bootstrap discipline matters most on the longshots — wide bands on small point estimates collapse the Pick rate fast. On Australia the lower bound is 25%, which keeps the lower-bound gap at +5.3pp against the market — past +3pp, so the Pick clears. The Desk's posture is that calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures — we're not claiming the market is generally wrong, only that this side, on this fixture, looks mispriced. Selection is the dimension this verdict adds value on.

This number will move. Confirmed starting elevens, injuries, weather at the venue, and suspensions carried in from previous fixtures all re-enter the prior on the late-binding cadence. With kickoff roughly 31 days out, the model is on the weekly refresh cadence; we'll move to daily once we cross the T-5d window. The Pick can flip to a Pass if news moves enough of the prior. The Desk does not tip and does not recommend a trade — the model price, the market price, and the gap across them are what's on the page.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives Australia a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +10.5pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: The model thinks Australia are mispriced. Our number reads 31% on the away side; the market reads 20%. The +10.5pp gap is the Pick.
copy.title: United States v Australia · the model leans Australia
